title: Sharpie Kraft — Design Sprint Brainstorm Wall
description: A butcher-paper brainstorm wall recreated in slides — kraft fiber texture, chunky Sharpie headlines, and four pastel sticky-note clusters wired together by hand-drawn marker arrows. Feels like mid-workshop chaos, entirely by design.
philosophy: This template believes that thinking out loud deserves a visual language as rough as the ideas themselves. It rejects the clean, finished deck that signals closure when the work is still generative and messy. Built for the whiteboard room — not the boardroom — it invites audiences to lean forward, grab a marker, and push the thinking further. Every imperfect stroke is a deliberate signal that iteration, not polish, is the currency of this room.
goodFor: Design-thinking workshop openers and team brainstorm kickoffs
Problem-framing slides with sticky-note theme clusters and connecting arrows
Innovation sprint retrospectives surfacing and grouping raw insights
Affinity mapping results presented live in cross-functional team reviews
avoidFor: Executive board decks requiring formal, polished visual authority
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews with dense KPI tables
Client-facing pitch decks for conservative industries such as finance or legal
High-resolution print handouts where paper-texture artifacts read as print defects
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Raw workshop-wall energy: the title lands like a decisive Sharpie sweep on torn kraft paper — asymmetric, confident, and visibly hand-done. Scattered pastel sticky-note shapes at the periphery signal invitation rather than conclusion, turning the opening slide into a live prompt. Keep every edge slightly imprecise and every element feeling placed by hand; clean geometry or centered symmetry would break the generative spell.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8% outer margin; headline text occupies columns 1–8, left-aligned and dropped into the upper third of the canvas. A loose cluster of two to three overlapping pastel sticky-note shapes occupies the lower-right corner as balancing visual weight, with one sweeping hand-drawn arrow looping back toward the title zone. Subtitle or workshop session label sits flush-left beneath the headline, separated from it by a rough horizontal marker-stroke rule. No header band; page identifier, if any, appears bottom-left at minimum size.

examples.promptCore: Mid-workshop brainstorm energy — a kraft-fiber background that reads like real butcher paper tacked to a wall. Four pastel sticky-note clusters drift at slight, irregular rotations, each anchored by a bold marker headline with rough jottings inside. Loose, imperfect arrows in dark marker ink trace live relationships between clusters, signaling in-progress thinking over finished conclusions. Avoid mechanical alignment or corporate polish — every element should feel placed in the moment, not composed after the fact.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid divided into four loose quadrants — top-left (cols 1–5), top-right (cols 7–12), bottom-left (cols 1–5), bottom-right (cols 7–12) — each quadrant hosting one pastel sticky-note block rotated a few degrees off-axis to simulate hand-pinning. Gutters between quadrants (cols 6 and the horizontal midline) are occupied by hand-drawn connector arrows that snake diagonally, not orthogonally. Each sticky block carries a chunky marker label as its theme header, with two to four short jotted lines below. No footer band; a small tally or corner scrawl anchors bottom-right, outer margin bleeds into the kraft texture with no clean rule line.
